title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 214: Beyond the Double Helix: Epigenetics
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 214 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Beyond the Double Helix: The Epigenetics Revolution

Paragraph 1. In 1953, two scientists named James Watson and Francis Crick found the spiral shape of DNA. For fifty years, doctors believed DNA was like a fixed plan written in stone. They thought the genes from your parents decided your future health completely, and nothing could ever change that plan.

Paragraph 2. Today, a new science called epigenetics shows a different story. Epigenetics studies how genes turn on or off without changing the DNA letters inside cells. Scientists compare the body to a computer. DNA is the computer hardware, which stays the same in every cell. Epigenetic marks are like computer software that tells each cell which programs to run or stop.

Paragraph 3. Daily habits and the environment around us can move these gene switches. Heavy stress, dirty air, regular exercise, and your daily diet all send signals to these marks. Even more surprisingly, parents can pass some marks to their children. During a severe food shortage in the Netherlands in 1944, pregnant mothers starved. Decades later, doctors found health changes in both their children and their grandchildren.

Paragraph 4. Because epigenetic marks can be turned back, doctors are making helpful new medicines. Some new drugs switch helpful protective genes back on to fight cancer cells without hurting healthy body cells. This shows our daily choices truly matter for our health.
